findings.title: No structured data (schema.org JSON-LD) on homepage
findings.evidence: No <script type='application/ld+json'> tags were found in the page HTML.
findings.should_be: At minimum, Organization and WebSite schema should be present.
findings.fix:
Add this to your homepage <head> (replace the placeholders):

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Your Business Name",
  "url": "https://yoursite.com",
  "logo": "https://yoursite.com/logo.png",
  "description": "One sentence describing what your business does.",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://twitter.com/yourhandle",
    "https://www.linkedin.com/company/yourcompany",
    "https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/yourcompany"
  ]
}
</script>

Tip: if you use WordPress, plugins like Yoast SEO or RankMath can generate this automatically. If you use Webflow, it's under Page Settings > Schema Markup.

findings.title: AI does not mention 'Example Domain' in any test queries
findings.evidence: Sent 3 questions to an AI model about document management and 'Example Domain'. The AI did not mention 'Example Domain' in any response. This means the model likely has no strong knowledge of your business in its training data.
findings.should_be: An AI should be able to describe what Example Domain is and mention it when asked about document management.
findings.fix:
The AI model has no knowledge of Example Domain. To fix this, you need to build presence on the sources AI engines learn from during training:

1. Create/maintain a Wikipedia page (if notable enough)
2. Ensure a Crunchbase profile with accurate description
3. Get listed on review platforms (G2, Capterra, TrustRadius)
4. Publish on high-authority industry blogs and publications
5. Build backlinks from sites that appear in AI training data
6. Ensure your homepage clearly states what you do in the first sentence

AI models are trained on web content — the more high-quality sources that describe Example Domain accurately, the more likely AI engines will mention you in their answers.

Here's a comparison of the leading document management platforms and their standout features:

## **Microsoft SharePoint**
- Deep integration with Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, Teams)
- Robust workflow automation through Power Automate
- Enterprise-grade security and compliance tools
- Strong intranet and collaboration capabilities
- Best for: Organizations already in the Microsoft ecosystem

## **Google Workspace (Drive/Docs)**
- Real-time collaborative editing
- Simple, intuitive interface with minimal learning curve
- Strong search capabilities across content
- Built-in AI features (Smart Compose, summaries)
- Best for: Teams prioritizing ease of use and real-time collaboration

## **Dropbox Business**
- Excellent file syncing and sharing
- Dropbox Sign for e-signatures
- Paper for lightweight document collaboration
- Strong third-party app integrations
- Best for: Creative teams and external file sharing

## **Box**
- Superior security and compliance certifications (HIPAA, FedRAMP, etc.)
- Advanced workflow automation (Box Relay)
- Metadata-driven content management
- Developer-friendly API ecosystem
- Best for: Highly regulated industries (healthcare, finance, government)

## **M-Files**
- AI-powered metadata tagging (no folder hierarchies needed)
- Automatic document classification
- Strong records management
- On-premises and cloud deployment options
- Best for: Organizations wanting to escape folder chaos

## **DocuWare**
- Focused on invoice processing and accounts payable automation
- Strong optical character recognition (OCR)
- Pre-built workflows for common business processes
- Best for: Mid-sized companies automating document-heavy operations

## **OpenText Documentum**
- Highly scalable for massive content volumes
- Strict governance and lifecycle management
- Industry-specific solutions (life sciences, energy)
- Best for: Large enterprises with complex compliance needs

**Key decision factors:** Microsoft/Google for collaboration, Box for security, M-Fi
